subject.title: [Bug]: cron.remove does not clean up session records in sessions.json

question: Should deleted cron jobs lose their base cron session immediately on `cron.remove`, or should base-row cleanup happen only through the guarded orphan-retention reaper?
rationale: Both choices are defensible: immediate cleanup fixes Control UI ghost sessions, while retention-only cleanup avoids erasing live-job preference state if the ownership boundary is wrong.

options.title: Pair direct remove with guarded reaper
options.body: Make `cron.remove` purge only the removed job's cron session artifacts, and keep the reaper responsible for older orphan rows with live-job safeguards.

options.title: Retention-owned cleanup only
options.body: Land the ownership-based reaper path and accept that deleted-job base sessions disappear after retention rather than immediately.

options.title: UI filters deleted jobs
options.body: Leave stored session rows intact and make the Control UI hide cron sessions that no longer map to a live job, preserving history at the cost of stale storage.

recommendation.title: Pair direct remove with guarded reaper
recommendation.body: Make `cron.remove` purge only the removed job's cron session artifacts, and keep the reaper responsible for older orphan rows with live-job safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cleanup boundary comes from the cron/session maintenance work he introduced and hardened.
